newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Traders wary of Bund rally, vols rise.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Traders wary of Bund rally, vols rise.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE rose on Thursday, as traders said the recent Bund rally may have set the scene for a move down in the underlying futures.
June Bund futures have risen from a low of 99.70 on April 14 to a high of 101.07 earlier in the session, and were at 100.99 at 1110 GMT.

"Yesterday's up move was particularly worrying," said a trader at a French house on the LIFFE floor. "The market has more than met its upside objectives, which makes many people think there will be a slide."
Bunds were boosted in part this session by the German Ifo economics institute survey, which showed that confidence in the economy was less strong than expected.
The west German business climate index fell to 92.4 in March, compared with 93.6 in February, far below expectations for a figure of 94.0.
"The market had already made its highs before the figure," said a trader at a major British brokerage in London. "There was a lot of talk that the figure was going to be weaker than the forecasts."
Although May options expire on April 23, traders said concerns that the fall in futures may be as soon as next week meant that May put options were still active.
May 99.50 strike puts had traded more than 1,500 by 1112 GMT, while the 100.00s had traded more than 1,800 and the 100.50s about 1,300.
Volatility for May was seen as high as 6.20 percent, up 0.10 from Wednesday, while June was up a similar amount at 5.80 percent.
Traders said June volatility was well-supported as a buying opportunity around the 5.5 percent level, where it was earlier in the week.
June puts were also active between the 99.00 and 101.00 strikes.
